Classic metrics of trait spacing and spread

Source: R/neighbour_metrics.R
neighbour_metrics.Rd

Metrics of the distribution of trait values within a community used in tests of community assembly: nearest-neighbour distances (Weiher et al. 1998; Stubbs & Wilson 2004), all pairwise distances, the minimum spanning tree, and the range and kurtosis (Cornwell & Ackerly 2009). Aiba et al. (2013) compared the statistical power of many of these metrics. Each function returns one number, so that it can be given as index to community_index(); with multivariate = TRUE there, the metrics of distances receive the matrix of traits of each site.

Usage

nn_distances(x, na.rm = FALSE)

mnnd(x, relative = FALSE, na.rm = FALSE)

sdnnd(x, relative = FALSE, na.rm = FALSE)

cvnnd(x, na.rm = FALSE)

min_nnd(x, relative = FALSE, na.rm = FALSE)

max_nnd(x, relative = FALSE, na.rm = FALSE)

mnd(x, relative = FALSE, na.rm = FALSE)

sdnd(x, relative = FALSE, na.rm = FALSE)

cvnd(x, na.rm = FALSE)

mst_length(x, relative = FALSE, na.rm = FALSE)

mst_ratio(x, na.rm = FALSE)

trait_range(x, na.rm = FALSE)

trait_kurtosis(x, na.rm = FALSE)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector (one trait), matrix or data frame (traits in columns, individuals or species in rows) or a dist object.

na.rm

Drop missing values (rows with any missing value of a matrix) before the computation; with FALSE (the default) missing values give NA.

relative

Divide by the range of the trait (one trait) or by the largest pairwise distance (several traits), as the div_range option of cati.

Value

A single number, or NA when there are too few values: two for the means, minima, maxima, the minimum spanning tree and the range, three for the standard deviations and coefficients of variation, four for the kurtosis. nn_distances() returns a vector with one distance per value (all NA when a value is missing and na.rm = FALSE).

Details

  • nn_distances(): distance from each value to its nearest neighbour (a vector).

  • mnnd(), sdnnd(), cvnnd(), min_nnd(), max_nnd(): mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation (sd / mean), minimum and maximum of the nearest-neighbour distances.

  • mnd(), sdnd(), cvnd(): mean, standard deviation and coefficient of variation of all pairwise distances.

  • mst_length(): total length of the minimum spanning tree; mst_ratio(): shortest over longest edge of the tree, as in MinMaxMST() of the package cati.

  • trait_range(): range of a single trait; trait_kurtosis(): excess kurtosis of a single trait (fourth standardised moment, with population moments, minus 3).

Distances are Euclidean among the rows of a matrix, or the absolute differences of a vector; a dist object (for instance Gower distances from cluster::daisy()) is used as it is. Identical values are at distance zero and count as such: an individual whose nearest neighbour has the same value has a nearest-neighbour distance of zero (cati discards zero distances). For a single trait the nearest neighbours and the minimum spanning tree are found from the sorted values, without the matrix of distances, so that large communities are fast.

Traits on different scales should be standardised over all communities before the metrics are computed (for instance with scale() on the whole data). Standardising within each community, as cati does by default, changes the units from one community to the next and between observed and null communities.

References

Aiba, M., Katabuchi, M., Takafumi, H., Matsuzaki, S. S., Sasaki, T., & Hiura, T. (2013). Robustness of trait distribution metrics for community assembly studies under the uncertainties of assembly processes. Ecology, 94, 2873–2885. doi:10.1890/13-0269.1

Cornwell, W. K., & Ackerly, D. D. (2009). Community assembly and shifts in plant trait distributions across an environmental gradient in coastal California. Ecological Monographs, 79, 109–126. doi:10.1890/07-1134.1

Stubbs, W. J., & Wilson, J. B. (2004). Evidence for limiting similarity in a sand dune community. Journal of Ecology, 92, 557–567. doi:10.1111/j.0022-0477.2004.00898.x

Weiher, E., Clarke, G. D. P., & Keddy, P. A. (1998). Community assembly rules, morphological dispersion, and the coexistence of plant species. Oikos, 81, 309–322. doi:10.2307/3547051

Examples

x <- c(1, 2, 2, 5, 9)
nn_distances(x)
#> [1] 1 0 0 3 4
mnnd(x)
#> [1] 1.6
mst_length(x)
#> [1] 8
mnnd(cbind(x, rev(x)))
#> [1] 3.449242
# as an index of communities against a null model
set.seed(1)
ind <- data.frame(site = rep(paste0("s", 1:5), each = 15),
                  species = sample(letters[1:4], 75, replace = TRUE), trait = rnorm(75))
community_index(ind, mnnd, null = "regional.ind", n_perm = 99)
#>   site trait index   observed        ses    p
#> 1   s1 trait  mnnd 0.21951480  1.5305257 0.12
#> 2   s2 trait  mnnd 0.11803015 -0.6224601 0.58
#> 3   s3 trait  mnnd 0.10781498 -0.9020233 0.42
#> 4   s4 trait  mnnd 0.06145019 -1.9225412 0.04
#> 5   s5 trait  mnnd 0.12445061 -0.4838972 0.70
